description.text: The last three cottages in Hollowbrook, and past them nothing but hedge and field. A ladder is still leaning against the first roof, which somebody's wife will have something to say about.

The lane peters out into a row of three cottages with the fields beginning immediately behind them — the far edge of the village. A ladder stands against the first roof with a bundle of reed lashed halfway up it. The second has more books in its window than the rest of Hollowbrook put together, and the third has a loom going in each of its two front rooms.

Three cottages at the far edge of the village, the fields starting right behind them. A ladder against the first, books stacked in the window of the second, and both front rooms of the third lit for weaving.
